claim: Under concurrent writers an append-only ledger admits exactly one entry per accepted append, with contiguous indices and an unbroken hash chain — a writer whose predecessor moved is rejected.

steps.label: two uncoordinated writers that both read the same head
steps.evidence: the hazard, staged as an explicit interleaving rather than a race, so it is deterministic
steps.note: Both entries claim the same predecessor. The chain no longer describes an order.

steps.label: 8 threads racing, each naming the head it built on
steps.evidence: 1 accepted, 7 rejected as head_moved; ledger holds 1 entry
steps.note: Exactly one wins. The assertion holds under every possible scheduling, so the test is not timing-dependent.

steps.label: 8 threads serialized through one lock

request.discipline: read head and extend under a lock

steps.note: No gaps, no duplicates, nothing lost — the other legitimate discipline.
